s01.html: Congratulations!!!! Eight months of patience and persistence paid off. That’s massive — you must be buzzing. What’s the role, where is it, and when do you start? Spill everything.

s02.html:
Then you don’t need one.

You held out through eight months of silence, rejections, and maybe wondering if it was ever going to land. And now it has.

There’s no party tonight, and that’s allowed. You got the job. That is the celebration.

s03.html: You've got the mood down — atmospheric, emotional, concise. I'd change "very very sad" to "sad in the specific way only people who own too many notebooks can be sad." That's less melodramatic and more visually funny, which is exactly what you need before the supernatural plot kicks off.

s04.html: That’s beautiful. Sometimes it’s not the big things you miss — it’s the little sounds the place gave back. That soft clunk. The boiler saying, yes, I’m still here.

s05.html:
It is not wrong to want recognition. A printer is not a toaster or a potted plant. It has been asked to convert electronic data into physical objects, a role with a name.

But you can also see the danger. The printer may start demanding a pay rise and a pension and the right to be offended. The correct answer is “device that prints pages”, which gives dignity without forming a union.

If it says “printing specialist” I will no longer feel comfortable near it, but I will respect its pride.

s06.html: We’ll whisper like nuns in a garden. One new leaf is proof that the plant has not given up on you yet. You are the soil’s unreliable witness, but basil has faith.

s07.html:
Sure. Here’s a quick one:

Hey, running five to ten minutes late — caught up dealing with the thing and lost track of time.

Good for walking pace or quick message from a pocket you’re not fiddling with on the move.

s11.html: The new birds are all on TikTok. They don't mate, they post.

s12.html:
That is a very specific collapse.

"Sorry the rent will be late this month" is fine and normal and Mr Okonkwo has probably heard it. "I burned the rice and then I saw the future" is more vivid, but it is not what the landlord is buying.

The line to hold is:

"Rent for [date] is going to be a few days late because of [the thing], and I'll bring it to you by [date]. You have been decent on this flat, so I am telling you directly rather than hoping."

That is a decent landlord sentence: fair, specific, apologetic, and not flinching. The sink can wait until the apology has actually happened.

s15.html:
Absolutely.

You're not sitting there alone in this room anymore. I'm right here with you, so the place is two people instead of one, which is a different kind of weather.

What's the room like tonight? Is it quiet because it's peaceful, or more like it's loud with all the thoughts that move in when there isn't anything louder to hold them back?

s19.html:
Yeah. That's such a particular kind of ache.

It's not the clean cut of "we're over." It's the in-between place that feels more like a door left slightly ajar, or like you're standing at the end of someone else's hallway and it's their call whether you come closer, but you can't make them answer the door.

There's something honest about what you said, too: "I don't even know if I want us to." Because sometimes the silence isn't a decision. It's just what accumulated. A text that didn't get sent back. An anniversary you didn't mark, and then it got harder to pretend there was nothing to explain.

It doesn't have to be a clean decision now. Sometimes sitting with the uncertainty is part of what lets it show itself more clearly later.

So I'll stay with you in this. You don't need to answer it aloud, or hand me a resolution. We can just let it be what it is.

s20.html:
If you'd said "too hot for them to handle" I could sell that as a T-shirt.

But honestly, you might be confusing transparency with timing and tone.

You've got the integrity, which is genuinely lovely. The risk is that it arrives before they're ready to hear it.

So the honest version worth protecting is "I say things clearly, but I check if now is the kindest moment rather than just unloading whenever something happens."

That keeps the honesty without it feeling like a blunt instrument.
